target.title: fix(diagnostic): avoid model-call stream hot-path object copies
target.body:
<!-- submission-timestamps:start -->
First submitted: July 2, 2026, 12:09 PM (US Eastern Time) / 16:09 UTC.
Last body edit: July 15, 2026, 3:31 AM (US Eastern Time) / 07:31 UTC.
Latest head commit: July 15, 2026, 3:09 AM (US Eastern Time) / 07:09 UTC.
<!-- submission-timestamps:end -->

Related: #91588
Related: #97211

## What Problem This Solves

This PR removes two object-copy patterns from model-call diagnostics while preserving the existing event and byte-accounting contracts:

- accumulated `partial` snapshots are excluded from response-byte accounting without reading the `partial` property;
- optional model-call event fields are assigned onto one event object instead of being built through conditional spread objects.

The contribution is intentionally narrow. It addresses one diagnostic hot-path allocation/read contributor and does not close or claim to resolve the broader, multi-cause gateway memory investigation in #91588.

The most useful validation is the [exact-head runtime proof](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29396515157), which shows byte-equivalent output, eight passing object-rest / JSON edge contracts, and `partialReads` dropping from `10000` on the official baseline to `0` on the PR head. The [current-head repository CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29396506599) also completed successfully.

## Breaking Changes

None expected.

## Why / User Impact

Long-running agent workloads can process many provider stream chunks. The previous diagnostic path created an object-rest snapshot for every non-delta chunk carrying `partial`, and destructuring read the excluded `partial` value before copying the remaining fields. The new helper avoids that read and avoids the snapshot allocation for common scalar data shapes while preserving diagnostic byte totals.

This changes internal diagnostic accounting only. It does not change provider transport, yielded stream chunks, model output, public configuration, persisted sessions, plugin state, or database/vector schemas.

## Implementation

- Move response-stream byte accounting into `attempt.model-diagnostic-byte-length.ts` so the serialization contract has a focused owner and test surface.
- Keep direct UTF-8 counting for text/thinking/tool-call deltas.
- Count common own-enumerable scalar data fields without allocating an object-rest snapshot.
- Fall back to an object-rest-equivalent copy for accessors, nested values, custom serializers, symbols, and other complex shapes.
- Preserve JSON omission behavior, value-level `toJSON(key)`, BigInt `toJSON(key)`, own-enumerable `toJSON`, source-object accessor receivers, and own-enumerable `__proto__` data keys.
- Keep inherited and non-enumerable `toJSON` excluded, matching native object-rest semantics.
- Build the base diagnostic event once and assign optional fields without conditional spread objects.

## Code-Path Analysis

- **Runtime entry point / caller:** `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream.ts` installs `wrapStreamFnWithDiagnosticModelCallEvents()` on the live agent stream function.
- **Owner:** `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.model-diagnostic-events.ts` owns model-call lifecycle observation and invokes the extracted byte-accounting helper for each observed chunk.
- **Callee:** `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.model-diagnostic-byte-length.ts` computes response byte totals and returns `undefined` rather than interrupting the provider stream when an opaque chunk cannot be inspected safely.
- **Adjacent contracts:** `src/infra/diagnostic-events.ts` owns emitted event delivery; `src/plugins/hook-types.ts` defines model-call hook fields; `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.model-diagnostic-events.test.ts` covers lifecycle, tracing, usage, hooks, progress, and completion/error behavior.
- **Focused regression tests:** `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.model-diagnostic-byte-length.test.ts` covers getter safety and the object-rest / JSON edge contract.
- **Stream contract:** the wrapper observes chunks but yields the original provider stream unchanged.

## Mainline Comparison

- The dedicated branch was rebased onto official `openclaw/openclaw:main@0d7da61e9b87a7aab67989866fc4cfdc888da1c1` before the final proof run.
- Official `main` advanced to `46fad5296a59ee6cfbd7b8e9b20bd9259cbe9e6f` while proof and CI were running. The seven intervening commits do not modify any of this PR's three files.
- Recent same-module changes, including Unicode-safe provider timeline attributes and the max-lines suppression ratchet, remain present after the rebase.
- Current `main` still uses object rest for `partial` exclusion and conditional spreads in the base event, so the narrow mitigation has not landed independently.

## Branch / Base Provenance

- Official base used for the final proof: `openclaw/openclaw:main@0d7da61e9b87a7aab67989866fc4cfdc888da1c1`.
- Dedicated PR head: `snowzlmbot/openclaw:fix/91588-diagnostic-stream-hot-paths@b6b63aca22c16a7760faeddd5367ef5b05de6526`.
- Dedicated evidence branch: `snowzlmbot/openclaw:proof/pr99154-model-diagnostic-runtime-ff6cbef@e460592297c273af9784d1fceb1693d5d664e0e3`.
- The fork default branch was not modified by this contribution. The evidence workflow and artifacts are not part of the PR code diff.

## Dependency / Contract Verification

- No dependency, lockfile, generated dependency graph, workflow, permission, secret, or package export change is included in the PR.
- Native object-rest and `JSON.stringify` behavior are treated as the compatibility baseline.
- The helper keeps the existing failure boundary: unsupported or opaque chunks omit the byte metric instead of failing the model stream.
- No persisted data model or migration is involved; the values are transient in-memory diagnostic events and plugin-hook payload fields.

## Labels Considered

`agents`, `P1`, compatibility risk, and availability risk are relevant because this is a per-chunk agent runtime path. Label application and final prioritization remain maintainer-owned.

## Validation

### Exact-Head Runtime Proof

- [Exact-head proof run](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29396515157) — `success`.
- Artifact: `pr99154-model-diagnostic-runtime-proof-29396515157-1` (`summary.md`, `baseline.json`, `head.json`).
- Environment: GitHub Actions `ubuntu-24.04`, Node `v24.18.0`, `workflow_dispatch`.
- Binding: official baseline `0d7da61e9b87a7aab67989866fc4cfdc888da1c1`; PR head `b6b63aca22c16a7760faeddd5367ef5b05de6526`.
- Harness source: dedicated evidence commit `e460592297c273af9784d1fceb1693d5d664e0e3`.

Exact-head edge results:

- unreadable accumulated `partial`: expected/actual `34 / 34`, `partialReads=0`;
- own non-enumerable `toJSON`: expected/actual `34 / 34`, calls `0`;
- inherited non-enumerable `toJSON`: expected/actual `34 / 34`, calls `0`;
- own enumerable `toJSON`: expected/actual `35 / 35`, snapshot receiver has no `partial`;
- string/symbol accessor receiver: source receiver preserved, expected/actual `34 / 34`;
- own enumerable `__proto__` data key: expected/actual `73 / 73`, `Object.prototype` unchanged;
- value-level `toJSON(key)`: expected/actual `68 / 68`, observed key `value`;
- BigInt `toJSON(key)`: expected/actual `52 / 52`, observed key `value`.

Runtime workload results:

- 50,000 representative chunks: baseline/head response bytes `2911669 / 2911669`.
- 10,000 accumulated-`partial` chunks: baseline/head `partial` reads `10000 / 0`; expected/head bytes `527780 / 527780`.
- Synthetic duration and RSS samples were noisy and did not show a stable improvement. They are reported in the artifact for transparency and are not used to claim a speedup, RSS plateau, or memory-leak resolution.

### Repository Checks

- [Current-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29396506599) — `success`.
- Code-push check-run read-back before the body-only proof updates: `70` success, `35` skipped, `1` neutral, `0` failed, `0` cancelled, `0` pending (`106` total).
- [Body proof gate after the required-section correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29397382821) — `success`. Three earlier body-only proof runs failed because the rewritten body used `## Summary` instead of the required `## What Problem This Solves` heading; the current body includes the required authored section and supersedes those failed attempts.

### Local Static Pre-Checks

- `git diff --check`
- `oxfmt --check` on the three changed files
- `oxlint` on the three changed files: `0` warnings, `0` errors
- max-lines suppression ratchet: passed

No local build or broad test suite is used as delivery evidence; repository build, type, lint, and test checks run in GitHub Actions.

## Evidence Source Map

- Exact-head runtime semantics and workload output: [proof run 29396515157](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29396515157), artifact `pr99154-model-diagnostic-runtime-proof-29396515157-1`.
- Current-head repository checks: [CI run 29396506599](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29396506599) and the PR check rollup.
- Field/native-stack evidence and the evolving multi-cause investigation: #91588.
- Earlier closed-unmerged candidate and its public review history: #97211.
- Focused compatibility coverage: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.model-diagnostic-byte-length.test.ts`.

## Sanitized Logs

```text
proof_run=29396515157 conclusion=success
baseline_sha=0d7da61e9b87a7aab67989866fc4cfdc888da1c1
head_sha=b6b63aca22c16a7760faeddd5367ef5b05de6526
baseline_partial_reads=10000
head_partial_reads=0
baseline_response_stream_bytes=2911669
head_response_stream_bytes=2911669
head_large_partial_expected_bytes=527780
head_large_partial_actual_bytes=527780
edge_contracts_passed=8/8
```

## Media Evidence

This is a headless, in-process byte-accounting path with no user interface or visual state. A screenshot would not establish byte equivalence, getter ordering, or stream preservation, and a screen recording would only restate terminal text. The linked Actions run and downloadable machine-readable baseline/head artifacts provide the inspectable full-flow evidence instead.

## Risk

- Arbitrary provider chunk objects can contain accessors, symbols, custom serializers, BigInt values, non-standard prototypes, or opaque proxies. Focused tests and exact-head proof cover the relevant object-rest / JSON boundaries.
- The helper runs for each observed chunk. A compatibility error could omit byte metrics; the outer error boundary prevents it from interrupting the model stream.
- Direct scalar counting trades native serialization allocation for explicit key/descriptor inspection. The proof establishes byte equivalence and eliminated `partial` reads, not a universal throughput or RSS improvement.
- #91588 contains other memory contributors and contradictory workload observations outside this module; they remain open and separately owned.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. No data rollback, schema migration, config change, or cache rebuild is required.

## Docs Updated

No user-facing documentation change is required because the patch changes internal diagnostic accounting only. This PR body documents the runtime contract, evidence, risk, and limitations.

## Related Issue / PR

- #91588 remains the canonical multi-cause gateway memory investigation. This PR is a non-closing candidate mitigation for one diagnostic hot path.
- #97211 is closed without merge and targeted the same two copy/spread sites. No reason for its closure is inferred here.

## Review Context Addressed

- Rebased the dedicated branch onto current official mainline and preserved intervening diagnostic changes.
- Moved byte accounting into a focused helper and kept the compatibility tests below the LOC threshold.
- Replaced the earlier proxy-oriented proof expectations with native object-rest semantics.
- Bound runtime proof to the exact final PR head and official baseline.
- Added explicit transient-data / no-migration reasoning.
- Reported the neutral/negative synthetic timing and RSS samples instead of presenting them as a performance win.
- Kept the contribution narrow and non-closing for #91588.

## Not Tested / Limitations

- No multi-day Gateway RSS, heap, allocator, or native-memory soak.
- No production workload or universal performance claim.
- No claim that this fixes threshold warnings, startup readiness, session/plugin retention, tool degradation, or all memory growth in #91588.
- No stable duration or RSS improvement was demonstrated by the exact-head synthetic run.
